message.content:
It’s hard to pin down a single “right” answer because the time depends on a handful of variables—crew size, equipment, weather, whether you’re doing a quick touch‑up or a full overhaul, and so on. Here’s a rough rule of thumb:

| Scope | Typical Crew Size | Hours/Day | Total Time |
|-------|-------------------|-----------|------------|
| **Full repaint (all exposed metal)** | 10–15 skilled painters + support staff | 8–10 hrs | ~2–3 weeks (≈80–120 man‑days) |
| **Partial repaint (selected sections)** | 5–8 painters | 8 hrs | ~1–2 weeks (≈40–60 man‑days) |

**Why this matters:**  
* The Eiffel Tower is actually repainted roughly every 7 years as part of its routine maintenance program.  
* A typical repaint uses a special anti‑rust primer followed by a protective topcoat; each layer needs drying time, so the schedule usually includes a few days between layers.  

So if you had a dedicated crew of 12 painters working standard shifts, you could expect a complete repaint to finish in about 2 weeks of active work (plus a couple of extra days for prep and curing). If you’re only touching up a few spots, you could cut that down to a week or less.
